# `⍤` — Atop / Rank / Axes

With function operand `g`, `f⍤g Y` is `f(g Y)` and `X f⍤g Y` is `f(X g Y)`.

```apl
2 -⍤+ 3            ⍝ ¯5
```

With numeric operand `R`, `f⍤R` applies to trailing cells of rank `R`. Frames use leading agreement. Results assemble with fill.

```apl
(+/⍤1)2 3⍴⍳6       ⍝ 6 15
```

| `R` | Monad rank | Dyad left/right ranks |
|---|---|---|
| `r` | `r` | `r r` |
| `q r` | `r` | `q r` |
| `p q r` | `p` | `q r` |

Negative ranks count back from argument rank. Excessive ranks clamp. Empty frames call the operand on prototype cells.

`∞` is the whole argument, and `¯∞` is rank 0. So `⍤1 ∞` pairs each row on the left with the whole right argument. That gives the matrix-vector product, which also multiplies matrices.

```apl
m←[1 2 3 ⋄ 4 5 6]
m +⌿⍤×⍤1 ∞⊢1 2 3                   ⍝ 14 32
m +⌿⍤×⍤1 ∞⊢[1 10 ⋄ 2 20 ⋄ 3 30]    ⍝ [14 140 ⋄ 32 320]
```

## Axes

With an enclosed operand, `f⍤[A]` applies `f` to the cells made of axes `A`. The other axes form the frame. Brackets are the usual way to write the operand, and they need no separator before the argument. Any enclosed value works.

```apl
{+/⍵}⍤[1]2 3⍴⍳6           ⍝ 5 7 9
ax←⊂1 ⋄ {+/⍵}⍤ax⊢2 3⍴⍳6   ⍝ 5 7 9
```

Rank is the case that selects the last `r` axes. The same digit points to opposite ends.

```apl
+/⍤1⊢2 3⍴⍳6              ⍝ 6 15
+/⍤[1]2 3⍴⍳6             ⍝ 5 7 9
```

Result cells with the same rank as the selected cells return to the axes `A`. Other result cells start at the position of the first selected axis.

```apl
{⌽⍵}⍤[1]2 3⍴⍳6           ⍝ ⊖2 3⍴⍳6
⍴{,⍵}⍤[1 2]2 3 4⍴⍳24     ⍝ 6 4
```

With two arguments, `A` applies to both, and leading frames agree as they do for rank. An argument without the selected axes is one whole cell, paired with every cell of the other argument.

```apl
1 0 1{⍺/⍵}⍤[2]2 3⍴⍳6      ⍝ [1 3 ⋄ 4 6]
10 20{⍺+⍵}⍤[1]2 3⍴⍳6      ⍝ [11 12 13 ⋄ 24 25 26]
```

The operand can name axes.

```apl
m←("row":2 ⋄ "col":3)⍴⍳6
{+/⍵}⍤["row"]m           ⍝ ("col":3)⍴5 7 9
```

### Exceptions

A primitive with its own axis meaning keeps it:

- Multi-axis reduce, including seeded reduce. `+/⍤[2 3]` flattens each cell before reducing.
- Partitioned enclose. `1 0 1 0⊂⍤[2]` cuts the whole matrix into blocks. Nest `⊆⍤[K]` follows the general rule. Both match Dyalog.
- Rotate with a count array. `1 2 3 4⌽⍤[1]` pairs one count with each column.
- Catenate and ravel with fractional positions, including laminate.
- Mix. `⊃⍤[A]` places the cell axes among the frame axes.
- Axis selectors. `⍳⍤[A]` returns the keys or positions of the selected axes.

```apl
+/⍤[2 3]2 3 4⍴⍳24        ⍝ 78 222
1 2,⍤[0.5]3 4            ⍝ [1 2 ⋄ 3 4]
```

A dfn has no axis meaning of its own, so wrapping a primitive in a dfn gives the general rule.

```apl
{+/⍵}⍤[2 3]2 3 4⍴⍳24     ⍝ [10 26 42 ⋄ 58 74 90]
```

## Errors

- `RANK`: a rank or axis operand that is not a scalar or vector
- `LENGTH`: a rank operand with more than three items
- `DOMAIN`: non-integral ranks, repeated axes, axes outside the higher-rank argument
